description: ASTROGENIX is a team of passionate innovators focused on space technology, AI, and healthcare innovation. Our goal is to develop a smart Health Monitoring App that makes health tracking easier and more accessible. We believe in creativity, teamwork, and using technology to solve real-world problems. We welcome enthusiastic team members skilled in Python, AI/ML, app development, UI/UX design, and data analysis. Together, we aim to innovate, collaborate, and make a meaningful impact!
summary: ASTROGENIX is an AI-assisted web dashboard for monitoring astronaut health on long space missions. It brings heart rate, blood oxygen (SpO2), body temperature and daily well-being check-ins (mood, stress, sleep) into one clear view. It shows trends over time, explains unusual changes in plain language, and raises configurable alerts when readings move outside set limits. It also flags missing or unreliable sensor data instead of presenting it as fact. The project addresses the challenge of creating health-monitoring software for astronauts, who face radiation, isolation, confinement and altered gravity far from medical care. It matters because it helps crews and mission teams notice early warning signs and review health status in one place. ASTROGENIX is an educational prototype that uses simulated data. It does not diagnose illness or replace medical professionals.
details:
ASTROGENIX is an AI-assisted web dashboard for monitoring astronaut health on long space missions. It has five pages: Dashboard, Live Monitoring, AI Health Analysis, Alerts, and History & Reports.

How it works: the user selects an astronaut profile, then enters or streams heart rate, blood oxygen (SpO2) and body temperature readings. They also log daily well-being (mood, stress, sleep, fatigue). Readings are checked for completeness, timestamps and configured ranges. Charts show trends over time, an AI-assisted module summarizes patterns and flags unusual changes in plain language, and an alert panel warns when a configurable rule is triggered. Users can review past records and export a report.

Benefits: physical and behavioral health are shown in one place, results are explained simply, and missing or unreliable sensor data is flagged instead of shown as fact. Thresholds are adjustable, and real sensors can be added later.

Goal: to show how health indicators, check-ins, trends and alerts can work together in one astronaut-focused interface, expandable with validated sensors and expert-reviewed requirements.

Limitations: this is an educational prototype that uses simulated data. It is not a certified medical device and does not diagnose illness or recommend treatment. AI output is decision support for review only.

Tools: Python, Pandas, Streamlit, Plotly, SQLite or CSV, and optionally Scikit-learn.

SI acknowledgement: the project idea and concept were created by our team. An AI tool (Claude) was used to help format the demo presentation slides and word some of the slide text.
